brief: Making decisions when you will never have enough information

slots.plotCapB: the part you pay for twice
slots.premise: The skill was never gathering. It is choosing well while the gaps are still open, and being honest that they stay open.
slots.standfirst: Every decision that matters gets made early, on partial evidence, by someone who would rather wait another fortnight. What follows is how to do that without dressing the delay up as research.
slots.r1v: It does not close. It moves, and it moves with you.
slots.r2v: Paid in weeks, and rarely counted anywhere.
slots.r3v: Can you name the one fact that would change the answer?

slots.gaugeLabel: the part that is knowable in advance
slots.aside: Some of the answer is not late. It has not been born yet.
slots.lede: Most of what you are waiting for does not exist. Whether the market wants it, whether the hire works out, whether the team can actually build the thing — these are not facts sitting in a drawer you have failed to open. They are made by the decision and they arrive after it.
slots.r1v: Precedent, prior art, what a thing costs today. Real, and worth one afternoon.
slots.r2v: Everything downstream of the commitment. No amount of reading produces it early.
slots.r3v: We treat the second kind as though it were the first, and call the wait diligence.
slots.pull: You cannot read your way to a fact that has not happened yet.

slots.gaugeLabel: what the first afternoon already bought
slots.aside: The curve flattens long before the anxiety does.
slots.lede: The first afternoon of looking moves you further than the following three weeks. After the knee in the curve you are buying reassurance at the price of accuracy, and the exchange rate is dreadful.
slots.r1v: Cheap, and they change the shape of the question you are asking.
slots.r2v: The same facts, restated by new voices. That is agreement, not evidence.
slots.r3v: Sources stop surprising you. The signal is to stop, not to widen the search.
slots.pull: Past the knee, more evidence buys comfort and calls it rigour.

slots.gaugeLabel: what you knew when the window shut
slots.aside: Delay feels free because it never appears on an invoice.
slots.lede: Choosing not to choose keeps the current arrangement in place, silently, with none of the scrutiny you would apply to a real proposal. It is still a position. It still has a price, and the price compounds.
slots.r1v: A status quo nobody has had to defend out loud in months.
slots.r2v: Weeks of the one input you can never buy back.
slots.r3v: Half the options you were protecting have closed by the time you look up.
slots.pull: A postponed decision is the default option, bought at full price.

slots.gaugeLabel: evidence that would actually move you
slots.aside: Most deliberation cannot say what would end it.
slots.lede: Stop asking whether you know enough. You never will, and the question carries no stopping rule. Ask instead which specific piece of evidence would make you choose differently — then look at whether you can get it this week.
slots.r1v: Go and get it. That is what research is for, and it takes a day.
slots.r2v: Decide now. Waiting for it has no end date attached.
slots.r3v: Then nothing you learn will move you, and the deliberation is a hiding place.
slots.pull: A question with no stopping rule is not a question.

slots.gaugeLabel: what more waiting could still buy
slots.aside: The same caution applied to everything is simply slowness.
slots.lede: The variable that should set your pace is not how important the decision feels. It is what leaving costs. A choice you can walk out of in a fortnight deserves an hour. One you will live inside for three years deserves the slow, expensive kind of thinking.
slots.r1v: Decide in the meeting. Doing it returns better information than studying it.
slots.r2v: Slow down and pay for evidence. This is where the research earns out.
slots.r3v: Treat the waiting as the work, and stay willing to walk away entirely.
slots.pull: Speed is not a virtue. It is a setting, and the exit sets it.

slots.gaugeLabel: how well you can judge your own exits
slots.aside: A framework for deciding is mostly a framework for feeling ready.
slots.lede: Everything above leans on reversibility, and reversibility is something we assert rather than test. You can cancel the contract. You cannot un-tell the team what you thought of them. Organisations keep the shape of a decision long after the decision is formally undone.
slots.r1v: Hires, structures and code outlive the choice that produced them.
slots.r2v: When being wrong has no floor, deciding quickly is not brave, it is careless.
slots.r3v: Sometimes the disciplined move is refusing the bet, not taking it faster.
slots.pull: None of this makes you right. It stops you calling the delay research.

slots.lede: The missing information is not coming. What arrives instead is a deadline, a rough sense of the shape, and the certainty that anything you learned next would have landed after the moment had passed.
slots.rule1: Name the fact that would change the answer, then fetch it or stop looking.
slots.rule2: Set the pace by what leaving costs, never by how large the decision feels.
slots.rule3: Say plainly that you are guessing. It is the only part of this that stays honest.
slots.last: Certainty was never on the table. Only the timing was.
slots.commitText: The evidence you were waiting for sits downstream of the choice. It starts arriving the hour you commit and not one minute before, which is why the people who look decisive are usually just further through the same fog.
slots.commitEnd: Move, and the ground gives you something to read.
